title: Unescaped trailing control characters break structured-output parser across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers reported intermittent JSON parsing failures when using function/tool calling with structured output. Failures appear at end-of-response boundaries (streaming or non-streaming) where the tool output contains trailing non-printable control characters (examples: ASCII 0x03 ETX, 0x1E RS). The downstream structured-output parser rejects the payload, causing the API to return a 500 or a structured-parse error to customers. This reproduces across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but is more frequent for customers using streaming+proxy layers or legacy agent-side adapters.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a chat request with a tool that returns structured JSON plus a binary attachment encoded in base64 where the base64 string ends with padding that includes a control byte when decoded by some client adapters.
2) Use streaming response path (chunked HTTP/2 or server-sent events) and insert a small network delay between final chunks to exercise assemblers.
3) Observe final assembled payload contains trailing control characters (e.g., '\x03') after the closing '}'.
4) Call the structured-output parser; parser raises a parse error or throws in the runtime path and we surface 500 to the customer instead of graceful fallback/repair.
investigation: Initial triage shows three failure modes: 1) runtime streaming assembler concatenates last chunk with an extra one-byte marker added by some internal proxy for connection bookkeeping; 2) some customer SDKs include terminal escape characters in tool outputs that are not escaped before sending; 3) our structured-output validator treats any trailing non-printable as a hard parse error instead of attempting canonical trim or checksum-based validation. We reproduced locally by simulating a proxy that appends 0x03 as a trailing marker to the final chunk. This exercise only surfaced when assembler did not normalize NUL/CTRL bytes at boundaries.
root_cause: A combination of implicit protocol footers inserted by an internal streaming proxy and overly strict parser semantics. The runtime streaming reassembly layer assumed chunk boundaries could be concatenated without sanitization. At the same time the structured-output parser rejects any non-whitespace trailing bytes after the JSON terminator. The intersection of these behaviors allowed a single control byte to flip a successful parse into a hard error. The issue spans Hosted, Dedicated, and Private because the proxy/adapter code paths and parser are shared across deployment modes.
fix: Primary fix implemented: sanitize trailing non-printable control bytes during final chunk assembly in the runtime path while preserving valid base64 and escaped sequences. Update structured-output validator to allow a single configurable set of trailing control/whitespace characters and to attempt a canonical trim before failing. Add explicit handling so base64 blocks are validated separately and not altered. New unit and integration tests added to cover streaming boundary cases and adapter-proxy interactions.
rollback_plan: If the runtime change causes regressions, revert the assembler sanitization and enable a temporary parser-level tolerant mode flagged per-tenant (server-side toggle) while we iterate. We will notify impacted customers and roll back within the same deployment window. Revert steps documented in the PR and release notes.
deployment_plan: 1) Cut runtime-1.20-canary with sanitizer enabled for 5% of hosted traffic and a small dedicated test pool. 2) Run a 48-hour soak with synthetic traffic and reproduce customer scenarios. 3) Gradually ramp to 25% then 100% for Hosted; for Dedicated/Private, deliver patches and configuration instructions to on-prem agents and provide a hotfix bundle for customers with managed Dedicated clusters. 4) Post-deploy, run end-to-end functional tests against representative customer stacks.

Alert: query parser.parse_errors.trailing_control_bytes.count > 10 in 5m => P0 oncall escalation

Customer: MedSafe (Private) — air-gapped deployment saw same parse failure after their internal proxy update; ticket raised by customer on 2026-03-13

next_steps: Finish parser tolerant trim logic and add opt-in tenant config for strictness by 2026-03-16.
Run cross-team review with networking/proxy owners to remove insertion of marker bytes or make marker explicit and negotiate protocol change by 2026-03-20.
Prepare customer communication and KB article describing cause, mitigation, and how to validate SDKs by 2026-03-18.
Close loop with SEs for each impacted customer and confirm remediation or apply on-prem patch for Private deployments.
notes: Do not strip bytes inside validated base64 sections; rely on separate base64 checksum validation instead.
Edgecases observed when the final JSON chunk ends exactly at the boundary of a network frame; assembler must reassemble in canonical order before sanitization.
We should consider adding a lightweight protocol marker instead of silent trailing markers to avoid future ambiguity.
